content: The Netherlands Forensic Institute, known in Dutch as Nederlands Forensisch Instituut, serves as the national forensic institute of the Netherlands. It is situated in the Ypenburg district of The Hague. This institute operates as an autonomous division under the Dutch Ministry of Justice and falls within the Directorate-General for Law Enforcement. On July 30, 1945, the Dutch government made the decision to establish a Justice Laboratory. Three years later, on November 4, 1948, this laboratory was formally recognized as an independent department within the Ministry of Justice. In 1951, another similar institution was founded, named the Gerechtelijk Geneeskundig Laboratorium (Judicial Medical Laboratory). This institution was later renamed the Laboratorium voor Gerechtelijke Pathologie (Laboratory for Judicial Pathology). The first CEO of this laboratory was Dr. Jan Zeldenrust, a pathologist. On November 1, 1999, the two laboratories were merged to form the Nederlands Forensisch Instituut (The Netherlands Forensic Institute). Initially, the institute was located in Rijswijk, but in October 2004, it relocated to its current location in the Ypenburg district of The Hague.
